elaine: Quick heads-up — ran a small profiler across the host ingress path this morning. Seeing ~8–12µs/token added by tokenization + proto unpack on small requests, but worst for streaming tiny chunks (p95 jump).
kevin: yikes. any easy reproduction?
amit: what workload? short single-turn chat or long streaming?
elaine: mostly short single-turn (<=64 tokens) and a stream case where client sends 1–5 token frames. Repro steps: run local grpc loopback with 2000 qps synthetic.
kevin: can you paste the perf script you used?
elaine: sure — 
```
# micro-bench harness
./ingress_bench --host localhost:8081 --qps 2000 --payload small --streaming true --duration 60
perf record -g -p $(pgrep ingress_service) -o /tmp/perf.data
perf script | stackcollapse-perf.pl > out.folded
./flamegraph.pl out.folded > flame.svg
```
kevin: flame shows heavy stacks in grpc::Writev + utf8-normalize + tokenizer::parse_token_span. writev syscall shows many small writes (<=256B).
bench-bot: automated-run: ingress_bench/streaming_smallframes — baseline(2026-03-10): p99=34ms p50=9ms; current: p99=57ms p50=17ms (+68% p99)
amit: sounds like fragmentation + syscall overhead. KV cache hits also droppping?
elaine: yup. KV cache hit-rate dipped ~6% during the microburst window because shards got hot and our prefix aggregator delayed request completion. Trace snippet: 
```
TRACE 0.012s ingress recv frame -> tokenize (8.9µs) -> proto_unmarshal (3.2µs) -> kv_lookup (sync wait 1.6µs) -> kvcache miss path (12.4µs) -> enqueue to runtime
```
maria: two quick hypotheses: 1) small gRPC writes cause more syscalls — coalesce on host side; 2) tokenization path is allocating per-frame; consider a pooled tokenizer and prefix-copy avoidance.
kevin: agree. also kernel selection interacts: small batches push runtime to select low-latency kernel variants but host overhead dominates, so auto-batcher thinks it's inefficient.
elaine: noted. I tried a quick experiment toggling a host coalescer (buffer up to 1KB or 5ms) — p99 dropped from 57ms -> 28ms, p50 from 17ms->8ms on that harness. No correctness issues in tests.
amit: nice. any regressions for long payloads?
elaine: minimal — added 0.5% tail for large (>=1k tokens) in the synthetic run because of the 5ms window, but throughput improved overall.
kevin: tradeoff seems acceptable for interactive workloads. We should also examine kvcache shard hotness — if kvcache misses drive enqueueing jitter, coalescing won't fully fix p99.
maria: action plan suggestion:
- elaine: land host writev coalescer behind feature flag + perf tests (owner: elaine)
- kevin: add tokenizer pool + reduce per-frame allocations in tokenizer (owner: kevin)
- amit: run kvcache hotspot simulation and try shard smoothing and prefetch (owner: amit)
- bench-bot: run canary nightly with small-frame streaming profile and report regressions to #eng-runtime
elaine: I'll open a short PR this afternoon and attach microbench results + flame svgs.
kevin: also add a telemetry gauge for "small_write_coalesced_bytes" and "tokenizer_allocs_per_request" so we can monitor in prod.
amit: good. if kvcache smoothing is nontrivial, we can short-term increase shard count for affected customers.
maria: ping @everyone — if we agree, let's schedule a 30m sync tomorrow to triage PR+bench results. :+1:
elaine: thanks folks. I'll post the PR link and attach flamegraph + perf raw data.
bench-bot: note: nightly canary scheduled at 02:00 UTC, will include ingress_smallframe profile.
